I will keep it simple and stay with the cropping pattern I trust most here in Quzhou County: winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same land. That is what fits my place, my age, and the weather best. I know this rotation, I can manage it without taking big risks, and it gives me steady grain from one year to the next. I would not spread myself into labor-heavy or uncertain cash crops. I would use improved wheat seed and hybrid maize seed because I want stable emergence, better yield, and stronger resistance. I would fertilize enough to protect yield but not chase the very highest output, because I care more about a dependable harvest than extra field work and extra cost. For wheat, I would topdress nitrogen once after greening and irrigate at the key stages. After wheat harvest, I would move quickly into summer maize, keep tillage light, give fertilizer in base plus topdressing, irrigate when the crop is under real pressure, and spray only when weeds, insects, or disease actually justify it. I am assuming I am managing 10 mu of ordinary irrigated farmland, and I am using the same 10 mu for the wheat-maize double crop system.
